title: Plant Leaf Tooth Feature Extraction
author: Wang Hu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wrxfd7n

steps.title: Image Preprocessing
steps.instruction: Convert the leaf image to a binary format through grayscale conversion, segmentation, and smoothing.

substeps.instruction: Convert the image to grayscale using the weighted average method.
Binarize the image using the maximum interclass variance method (OTSU).
Perform closing operations to fill small holes and gaps.
Smooth and denoise the image using a disc struct radius.

steps.title: Leaf Edge Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract and refine the leaf edge to identify corner candidates.

substeps.instruction: Extract the leaf edge using the Canny operator with thresholds H and L.
Perform single pixelization of the leaf edges.
Judge the contour curve open-close status based on the Gap_size threshold.
Apply periodic convolution smoothing for closed curves, or convolve open curves with a Gaussian function.
Calculate the curvature of all points on the curve; define points with maximum local curvature as corner candidates.
Adaptively calculate threshold C based on average curvature in the ROS region and remove corners with curvature less than C.
Calculate the angle of remaining candidates based on the dynamic support region and remove those with an angle smaller than parameter T_angled.
Compare corner point positions with open curve endpoints; mark endpoints as candidate corners if they are far apart.

steps.title: Identify Convex and Concave Points
steps.instruction: Determine if a corner point is convex or concave based on local point density.

substeps.instruction: Set a circle with radius L centered at the corner point.
Calculate the number of target points and background points within the circle.
Classify the point as a convex point if the number of target points is less than the number of background points.

steps.title: Analyze Tooth Length and Order
steps.instruction: Determine the length and hierarchical order of the leaf teeth.

substeps.instruction: Calculate tooth length as the distance from the convex point to the line formed by adjacent concave points.
Normalize teeth length by dividing by the length of the longest tooth (excluding abnormal points > 2x the mean length).
Count teeth with length < 0.5 of the maximum length; if this count is > 50% of total teeth, the leaf has two orders of teeth, otherwise one.
For two-order leaves, distinguish first-order teeth (significantly larger than two adjacent teeth) from second-order teeth.

steps.title: Analyze Tooth Spacing
steps.instruction: Evaluate the regularity of the spacing between adjacent teeth.

substeps.instruction: Calculate tooth spacing as the distance between adjacent teeth.
Compare minimum intertooth distance (dmin) with maximum intertooth distance (dmax).
Classify as regular if dmin > (dmax * 0.6), otherwise classify as irregular.

steps.title: Calculate Total Tooth Count
steps.instruction: Determine the total number of teeth by counting the total number of detected convex points.

steps.title: Determine Concave Shape Curvature
steps.instruction: Establish a curvature threshold to distinguish between rounded and angular concave shapes.

substeps.instruction: Calculate curvature at concave points of leaves with rounded concave shapes.
Calculate curvature at concave points of leaves with angular concave shapes.
Determine the curvature threshold value based on the statistical data from the previous two steps.

steps.title: Classify Tooth Shape
steps.instruction: Classify the tooth shape as CV, CC, FL, or RT using polynomial fitting and pixel analysis.

substeps.instruction: Extract coordinates of an arc between a concave point and a convex point on the profile curve.
Fit the coordinates to a quadratic polynomial.
If the quadratic parameter is zero, the shape is straight; if nonzero, proceed to pixel analysis.
Connect concavo-convex points with a straight line and count black (0) and white (1) pixels in the closed area between the line and the contour.
If intersection point C does not exist: compare black pixels (n0) and white pixels (n1) in the area; if n0 > n1, shape is CV, otherwise CC.
If intersection point C exists: divide the area into region P and region Q. Determine if P and Q are 'Black' (n0 > n1) or 'White' (n1 > n0).
If P is Black and Q is White, shape is RT; if P is White and Q is Black, shape is FL.
